probes.description: flow.inputSchema.required is enforced before any step runs: PlaceWidgetOrder with only customerEmail is refused with INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED naming both missing fields, while a complete body is not refused for input reasons.

steps.name: positive control: complete body passes input validation (flow may fail LATER, see fl-generated-action-completes)

probes.description: flow.inputSchema property constraints (type integer, minLength 1) are enforced: a string lineCount gives type_mismatch, a fractional lineCount gives type_mismatch, an empty customerEmail gives min_length.

An invariantCheck step with invariants [CustomerEmailRequired, LineCountNotNegative] on scope WidgetOrder stops the flow with INVARIANT_FAILED / 422, names LineCountNotNegative, the concept and the step, and no later step (save-order) runs.

steps.name: execution never reached save-order (no 'saved' in flow state)

probes.description: invariantCheck with checkpoint 'pre' in UpdateOrderLineQuantity refuses quantity 0 (PositiveQuantity, stepIndex 0) BEFORE apply-quantity runs: the stored line keeps its old quantity; a valid quantity passes and is stored.
forEach over $input.entries runs (2-item and 500-item collections succeed), refuses a missing collection with a message naming the step and path, and refuses 501 items against maxLoopIterations=500.

$.error.matches: forEach step sweep-entries requires an iterable collection at [$]input[.]entries

probes.description: A capabilityCall step (notification.send) is dispatched to the bound in-process notification adapter: the flow result carries the adapter id and channel the dispatcher selected. Surprising-but-actual: the adapter's metadata is merged into the returned $input.

return step yields exactly $input (nested structure preserved); callProcedure resolves the procedure's own return (RenameOrderStatusProcedure returns the client-supplied newStatus) and a missing procedure input fails the flow with REF_UNRESOLVABLE naming newStatus.

PlaceWidgetOrder's generatedAction step ScoreWidgetOrderRisk names a procedure declared in the model, so it runs that procedure (REG-259; before, it failed with capability_not_found AFTER save-order had written the row). POST /api/flows/PlaceWidgetOrder/execute with a valid body finishes OK and returns the saved order (outputSchema id/customerEmail/status/lineCount).

flow.startEndpoint=true is surfaced by the running app: the OpenAPI operation for POST /api/v1/flows/PlaceWidgetOrder/execute (and its specializing flow) carries x-npdev-start-endpoint=true; RecordOrderLines (flag absent) and ConfirmWidgetOrder do not.

Saga compensation: when a LATER step fails, the onFailure block of the already-completed save-order step runs (compensate-notify capabilityCall) -- its output variable compensationNotice and the durable __npdev_compensatedSteps__ counter are in the failed execution's state. The forcing failure is reject-unscorable-order (index 6): an order with lineCount 99 reaches a generatedAction (UnimplementedRiskPolicy) that no procedure or packaged code implements, so it fails with a capability binding error after save-order completed.

steps.name: control: nothing to compensate when save-order never completed

probes.description: After a compensated failure the execution monitor (GET /api/executions/history, documented 'COMPENSATED' when an onFailure block ran) reports compensationStatus COMPENSATED and compensatedSteps >= 1 (REG-260: the redacted execution the monitor reads used to mask the platform's compensation counter, so it said NONE / 0). Forcing failure = lineCount 99 (reject-unscorable-order).

PlaceWidgetOrderAudited declares only 'specializes' + hooks, yet it enforces the parent's inputSchema (required fields) and the parent's validate-order invariantCheck (LineCountNotNegative at stepIndex 0).

The 'after save-order' flowHook of PlaceWidgetOrderAudited injects its emitEvent step right after save-order: the execution emits WidgetOrderPlaced from step hook-emit-placed at stepIndex 2 (validate=0, save=1), carrying the saved order; the parent flow without the hook completes and emits WidgetOrderPlaced only once, from its own scheduleEvent step announce-order-placed, never from hook-emit-placed.

steps.name: event is persisted in the event store
control: parent flow (no hook) emits only its own announce-order-placed event

probes.description: orchestrationRule PushNewOrdersToErp (trigger event WidgetOrderPlaced) starts when a FLOW emits WidgetOrderPlaced: an OrchestrationStarted event whose payload.sourceEventId is that exact event appears. PlaceWidgetOrderAudited emits WidgetOrderPlaced twice (the hook's emitEvent, then the parent's announce-order-placed), so the two newest OrchestrationStarted events name those two events (in either order: both start within the same millisecond, so 'newest first' does not order them). A flow event with another name (WidgetOrderLineRecorded) starts no orchestration. (The rule's webhook action targets 127.0.0.1:9099 which is not served here, so its action outcome is deliberately not asserted.) Relies on probes running sequentially: the OrchestrationStarted list is read newest-first.

steps.name: control event of a different name
orchestration started for the emitted event
no new orchestration for a non-matching event

probes.description: emitEvent step in RecordOrderLines emits WidgetOrderLineRecorded after the line is saved (stepIndex 2, step emit-line-recorded) and persists it in the event store under the execution's correlation id; a run refused by invariantCheck emits and persists nothing.

awaitEvent with match.correlation=true parks AwaitPaymentConfirmation (HTTP 202, WAITING_EVENT, awaited event/step/correlation reported); a PaymentConfirmed event with a DIFFERENT correlation id leaves it waiting; the event carrying the execution's correlation id completes it.

steps.name: still waiting after the unrelated event
publish with the awaited correlation id

probes.description: A (sequential) forEach containing awaitEvent parks once per item: ProcessWidgetOrderLineApprovals over 2 skus awaits correlation '<exec>::forEach:await-line-approved:0' first; the iteration-0 event moves it on to wait for iteration 1 (still WAITING_EVENT); only the iteration-1 event completes the flow. An empty collection completes immediately without waiting.

steps.name: completed after the last iteration event

probes.description: parallelAwait forEach starts every iteration at once (the map step of BOTH iterations ran before any event: skuSeen exists for 0 and 1), needs ALL iteration events (after the event of iteration 0 alone the execution stays WAITING_EVENT, iteration 0 consumed, and an explicit resume changes nothing), and the event of the last outstanding iteration completes the flow by itself (REG-261) with each iteration's emitEvent WidgetOrderLineApprovalRecorded persisted under its own iteration correlation id.

steps.name: map output of iteration 1 exists while still waiting
iteration 0 was consumed by its own event; iteration 1 is still outstanding
resume with one of two events: join not satisfied
the last outstanding iteration's event completed the execution by itself
iteration 0: the awaited event plus the event it emitted
iteration 1: the awaited event plus the event it emitted

probes.description: For a parallelAwait forEach, publishing the awaited event for EVERY iteration (POST /api/events/publish, correlation '<exec>::forEach:await-line-approved-parallel:<i>', i=0,1) resumes the execution to COMPLETED just as a single awaitEvent does (see fl-await-event-resumes-only-on-matching-correlation), with no explicit /resume (REG-261: the parked iterations' wait descriptors were stored where the event-arrival lookup never looked).

steps.name: execution completes after the last awaited event

probes.description: approvals::RequestApproval awaits ApprovalDecided with match.payload requestId=$saved.id: a decision for ANOTHER request id leaves it waiting and the request PENDING; the decision for this request resumes it, the branch condition $decision.status is truthy so the THEN arm (apply-decision) runs and the stored request becomes APPROVED with decidedBy/decisionComment filled in.

Branch step has-decision (condition $decision.status) takes the no-arm path when the condition is falsy: a matching ApprovalDecided event with an EMPTY status resumes and completes the flow, but apply-decision does NOT run -- the request stays PENDING with no decidedBy. (Contrast: fl-await-payload-match-and-branch-then-arm.)

The awaitEvent step AwaitCatalogEntryApproval carries a humanTask assigned to role WarehouseManager. The probe actor (ADMIN, not WarehouseManager) is not an assignee: the task is absent from GET /api/tasks, GET /api/tasks/<id> is 403 TASK_FORBIDDEN (404 TASK_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id proves the 403 is the role check), completing it is 403 and the parked execution stays WAITING_EVENT. The assignee-side path (complete -> outcome event) needs a WarehouseManager principal and is not reachable with the single probe key.

steps.name: no open task is offered to a non-assignee
unknown task id is a different error

probes.description: createConcept (RecordOrderLines.save-line) really stores the row in the scope concept: the flow output id is readable through the concept REST API with the same field values and the derived lineTotal (quantity*unitPrice) computed.

A flow whose input is {concept, mode} is the write path of that concept: REST POST /api/widget_order_lines runs RecordOrderLines (create) and PUT /api/widget_order_lines/<id> runs UpdateOrderLineQuantity (update) -- the newest WidgetOrderLineRecorded event is emitted by the respective flow at its emitEvent stepIndex 2. Assumes no other client writes order lines between the write and the event read (probes run sequentially).

KNOWN DEFECT: createConcept in a flow bypasses the concept's required-field invariants. REST POST /api/widget_order_lines {sku, quantity} is refused 422 invariant_failed required(unitPrice)/required(widgetOrderId); the SAME body through POST /api/flows/RecordOrderLines/execute returns 200 OK and stores a line with widgetOrderId=null and unitPrice=null (observed: lineTotal 0/null). Expected: 422 INVARIANT_FAILED naming required(unitPrice).

steps.name: control: REST create refuses the incomplete line
flow createConcept must refuse it too

probes.description: KNOWN DEFECT: updateConcept replaces the whole row instead of merging. REST PUT {quantity} keeps sku/unitPrice/widgetOrderId (and bumps version), but POST /api/flows/UpdateOrderLineQuantity/execute {id, quantity:7} leaves the stored line with sku=null, unitPrice=null, widgetOrderId=null (data loss), version still 0. Expected: sku unchanged.

KNOWN DEFECT: a flow with input mode 'update' (UpdateOrderLineQuantity) given an id that does not exist should fail (404/409/422); ACTUAL: 200 OK and it silently CREATES a row with that id (sku/unitPrice/widgetOrderId null) that GET /api/widget_order_lines/<id> then returns. The REST PUT on a missing id is 404 (control).

steps.name: control: REST PUT on a missing id
flow update of an id that never existed

probes.description: REG-301: an emitEvent step's data mapping builds the event payload key by key (KernelRunner.buildEventPayload) instead of forwarding a whole reference. ShapeWidgetOrderLineEvent maps $input.orderRef -> widgetOrderId and $input.code -> sku, so the stored WidgetOrderLineShaped event carries exactly those renamed keys and not the input's own keys (orderRef, code, noise).

steps.name: payload carries the mapped keys only
